model: Project-stage risked NPV: probability-weighted unlevered DCF of Vulcan's attributable Lionheart lithium + geothermal flows, explicit construction capex and ramp (owner-FCF component engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case terminal growth; historical CAGRs are not a forward input for a pre-production project
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (51%) is capital raised, not retained earnings (EUR 586m of share issues in FY2025 alone); revenue 3yr CAGR (24.6%, FY2022 EUR 3.8m -> FY2025 EUR 7.35m) is Insheim power sales, unrelated to the lithium project. EPS and owner FCF are negative in every year, so their CAGRs are undefined. FY2019-FY2021 are AUD and FY2022+ EUR (disclosed presentation-currency change), so 5-year figures are not computed.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less interest income) FY2022 -47.5, FY2023 -122.2, FY2024 -103.7, FY2025 -105.3 (EUR m): construction-phase burn, not a trend to extrapolate. None of it informs the forward paths, which are built from the project parameters.

scenario_narratives.base: Lionheart Phase One is built broadly on the current schedule (commissioning and ~4kt in 2028, full 24ktpa from 2031) at a remaining net capex of ~EUR 1.2bn after EUR 204m of German grants, with opex 50% above the 2023 BES estimate and long-run lithium hydroxide at EUR 14k/t (~US$16k) — the consensus long-run range, well below the ~EUR 26k/t the BES revenue target implied. Vulcan's 70% attributable share of a ~EUR 200m EBITDA, ~EUR 150m owner-FCF asset, less its 70% share of the build, nets to roughly today's price. The axes that matter: whether VULSORB A-DLE hits design recovery and uptime at 100x optimisation-plant scale, the 2027-28 lithium price when offtake pricing resets, and whether the EUR 2.2bn package covers the build without another parent raise.
scenario_narratives.bull: Construction lands on the BES budget and the 2028 start, A-DLE performs to design (opex EUR 5,000/t), and a 2027+ supply deficit lifts realised LHM to EUR 20k/t with the offtakers (Stellantis, Umicore, LGES, Glencore) taking full volumes at an EU low-carbon premium. Lionheart's cash flow and the repeatable platform then fund Project Ludwig (PFS post-tax NPV8 EUR 1.7bn, 20% IRR) on a 2029 FID, adding ~21ktpa carbonate from 2033. Phase Two is the bulk of the bull upside and requires Phase One to work first — the bull needs two independent things to go right, hence the 20% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: A first-of-kind plant does what first-of-kind plants do: a one-year slip, a ~20% overrun, a plant that settles at 22kt, opex at EUR 7,000/t, against a lithium market still in surplus (EUR 11.5k/t). The project then earns below its cost of capital and the DCF equity is negative — i.e. existing shareholders are diluted or the asset is partly sold to complete. Permitting/legal (the Feb-2026 Nancy court annulment of the French geothermal permit) and a policy shift away from EU critical-raw-materials support are the tail behind this leg.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Development-stage project valued as a risked NPV: the explicit construction capex, ramp and steady-state economics of Vulcan's ~70% attributable share of Lionheart are modelled year by year on the owner-FCF component engine (SBC expensed, flat share count, interest income stripped, leases as debt), and execution/price/dilution risk is carried in the scenario flows and a 35% bear weight rather than in the discount rate. A 15-year horizon lets the terminal value capitalise a steady-state producing year. Historical FCF is construction burn and is not projected.
key_risks_to_valuation: A-DLE (VULSORB) recovery, uptime and reagent cost at 100x optimisation-plant scale: the base assumes opex 50% above the BES; the bear 75%
Realised lithium hydroxide price at the 2028-30 offtake resets: every EUR 1,000/t is ~EUR 24m of 100%-basis revenue (~EUR 17m attributable), almost all of it EBITDA
Schedule and cost: each year of delay costs a year of discounting plus ~EUR 40m of corporate burn; each 10% overrun is ~EUR 150m at 100%

Attributable share: PIK accruals on the PlatformCo preferred shares and any standby funding draw push Vulcan's economic interest below the 70% assumed; further parent equity (bear) would dilute the 481.7m count

Funding of the parent's 70% share of the build is the June-2026 cash (EUR 316m incl. deposits) plus the project debt; a covenant or drawdown-condition failure before first cash flow is the going-concern tail
Policy: EU CRMA Strategic Project status, Li4BAT grants and KfW/ECA/EIB participation are a large part of why the capital is available at all
FX: EUR flows against an AUD quote; a 10% EUR/AUD move is ~10% of the AUD value per share

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (VUL.AX) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.01-7.16; EURAUD=X and VUL.DE from the same endpoint on the same day for the fx parity check
data_sources.financials: VUL.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, EUR from FY2022; AUD FY2019-FY2021); H1 FY2026 Half Year Report (30 June 2026 balance sheet: cash note 7, other financial assets note 9, lease liabilities, NCI note 20, performance rights note 22, capital commitments note 23, financing package notes); FY2025 Annual Report (financing package composition p.20, Li4BAT grants, SBC note 39); FY2023 Annual Report (Phase One Bridging Engineering Study: EUR 1,399m capex, EUR 4,022/t opex, 24ktpa, EUR 705m target revenue)
data_sources.qualitative: VUL.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): FID Dec 2025, financial close May 2026, Project Ludwig PFS Sept 2026, offtake with Stellantis/Umicore/LGES/Glencore, Nancy court ruling Feb 2026

risked_npv_memo.summary: The engine weights the bear scenario's NEGATIVE DCF equity (equity_value EUR -343m, AUD -1.16/share) into probability_weighted.weighted_iv. That is the correct arithmetic for 'how much value the three paths create', but under limited liability a current shareholder's downside stops at zero: a negative DCF equity means the parent must raise dilutive equity or sell down the asset to complete, not that holders pay more in. The zero-floored (limited-liability) probability-weighted value is therefore also reported here as a memo; the canonical weighted_iv is the engine's unfloored figure.
risked_npv_memo.how_to_read: At AUD 1.115 the market is paying roughly the base case (AUD 1.13) and slightly above the unfloored weighted value (AUD 1.06); it sits below the floored weighted value (AUD 1.46). Both the base and bear hurdle entry prices are negative: at a 15% required return the project, as modelled, is not worth a positive price unless the bull leg (Phase One on budget plus a price recovery and Project Ludwig) is realised. The stock is a call option on first-of-kind execution and the 2028-30 lithium price, and should be sized as one.
risked_npv_memo.mechanics_note: Every scenario shows terminal_value_bound = cap (12x) and implied terminal EV/EBITDA of ~8x; terminal_pct_of_value exceeds 100% in the base case because the explicit-period PV is negative (construction capex), which is expected for a pre-production project, not a model fault.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, consolidated statement of profit or loss, 'Share-based payments expense' note 39 (EUR 4,564k); equity-award taxes nil (performance rights settled by share issue, no net-share withholding)
inputs.fx_note: EUR->AUD 1.6222 (Yahoo EURAUD=X, 2026-11-06). Parity check against the Frankfurt listing: VUL.DE EUR 0.715 x 1.6222 = AUD 1.160 vs VUL.AX AUD 1.115 observed (3.9% gap; the FSE print is ~11 hours after the ASX close on a stock with a 1.01-7.16 52-week range, so the gap is session timing, not a quote-basis error). All flows and per-share values are computed in EUR and converted at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are AUD to match current_price.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T05:10:27Z ASX regular close (Yahoo chart API); 52-week range 1.01-7.16
inputs.share_count_basis: 478.661m ordinary shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 report) plus 3.028m performance rights on issue (note 22) = 481.689m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The strategic/KfW project equity is minority interest at subsidiary level, not Vulcan shares, and is handled through the 70% attributable share of flows (see nci_treatment). A bear-case outcome would require fresh parent equity (dilution) that is not in the count; that is the finding, not a modelling omission.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate: 10y Bund ~2.7% + 1.6 beta x 5.5% ERP = ~11.5% cost of equity; EIB/ECA-backed project debt ~5.5% pre-tax (~4% after tax) at a ~40% steady-state D/V gives ~8.5%; rounded up to 9.0% for a single-asset, long-dated, construction-phase stream. Same 9% in all three scenarios: execution, pricing and schedule risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and the 35% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: EUR 30.666m lease liabilities (30 June 2026) added to total_debt; no lease charge inside EBITDA; right-of-use depreciation sits in the D&A path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows, no NCI deduction in the bridge (charged once). KfW holds 14.49% of Vulcan Energie Ressourcen GmbH (HoldCo) for up to EUR 150m; HOCHTIEF/Siemens FS/Demeter (via Sequana) hold 10.35% of VER GEO LIO GmbH (PlatformCo, the Lionheart project entity) for EUR 120m of a EUR 133m / 15% commitment, with PIK entitlements accruing to the earlier of completion or 30 June 2032 and converting into further PlatformCo shares. (1-0.1449) x (1-0.15) = 72.7% before PIK; ~70% after a 3-year PIK accrual. ALL project revenue, EBITDA and capex in every scenario are therefore scaled to 70% of the 100%-project figures stated in the scenario narratives, and the EUR 141.3m book NCI is NOT deducted (it would be a second charge, and book value badly understates the partners' claim on a completed project). Project Ludwig (bull only) sits under HoldCo but outside PlatformCo, so its true attributable share is ~85%; applying 70% there is deliberately conservative.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Vulcan is pre-revenue for lithium (FY2025 revenue EUR 7.35m is Insheim geothermal power/heat; owner FCF -EUR 105m), took FID on Lionheart Phase One in Dec 2025 and reached financial close on the EUR 2.2bn package in May 2026; first lithium targeted 2028. The dcf-methods routing table has no development-stage row, and a historical-ratio owner-FCF projection would be meaningless here, so the model is a project-stage risked NPV built on the owner-FCF component engine: year-by-year attributable revenue, margin and capex paths derived from the project parameters (24ktpa LHM, 560 GWh heat / 275 GWh power, BES opex EUR 4,022/t uplifted to EUR 5.0-7.0k/t for first-of-kind risk, BES capex EUR 1,399m escalated to EUR 1.45-1.9bn remaining, EUR 204m German grants netted against capex), with the construction/ramp/price/dilution risk carried in three scenarios and their weights. The bear case is the classic risked-NPV 'project fails to earn its capital' leg. ANCHORS: balance sheet and share count at 30 June 2026; FY2026 (year 1) flows are H2 FY2026 ONLY (H1 capex of EUR 168.8m and H1 operating burn are already inside the June cash), so year-1 capex is EUR 210m gross / EUR 170m net of grants at 100%. Cash includes EUR 80m term deposits >90 days, EUR 39.7m restricted cash and EUR 2.7m bank guarantee collateral held under the project financing (they fund the capex that is in the flows). The undrawn EUR 1,185m senior debt and the uncalled strategic/KfW equity instalments are financing of capex already in the flows and are NOT added to net cash. CURRENCY: statements changed presentation currency from AUD to EUR from FY2022 (disclosed); CAGRs are therefore computed on the EUR years only. Interest income (EUR 2.8m) stripped from the base and excluded from forward margins because the cash pile is in the bridge. Historical growth is NOT the growth driver here; selected_growth_rate is the base terminal growth. buyback_cash is zero and the flat count is a modelling convention the company has never funded. 15-year horizon so the terminal year is a steady-state producing year (FY2040), not a ramp year.

bear.narrative: 100%-project figures: first-of-kind scale-up problems push first lithium to 2029 and total remaining gross capex to ~EUR 1.9bn (+20%: 210/720/500/200/50 over 2026-30, net of grants 170/620/436/200/50); plant settles at 22kt not 24kt (4kt 2029, 12kt 2030, 20kt 2031, 22kt 2032); realised LHM EUR 11,500/t (~US$13k: the 2027 surplus persists and the offtake floors bite); opex EUR 7,000/t -> revenue EUR 298m and EBITDA ~EUR 99-105m (33-35%) from 2032; terminal growth 1%. Corporate burn EUR 38-40m/yr through the delay. This is the 'project does not earn its capital' leg of the risked NPV: the equity is worth less than nothing on a DCF basis, meaning the parent would need further dilutive equity (the Dec-2025 raise was at EUR 2.24; the stock is EUR 0.72) or a partner sell-down to complete.

base.narrative: 100%-project figures behind the 70%-attributable paths: revenue EUR 5m (2026), 6m (2027), 73m (2028: 4kt LHM at EUR 12k/t + EUR 25m energy), 253m (2029: 16kt at 13k + 45m), 358m (2030: 22kt at 14k + 50m), 388m (2031: 24kt at EUR 14k/t ~ US$16k, consensus-type long-run, + 52m energy), then +1.5%/yr. Opex EUR 6,000/t (BES 4,022/t + 50% first-of-kind/inflation) + EUR 15m energy opex + EUR 30m corporate; EBITDA -19m (H2 2026), -35m, -14m, 104m, 181m, 199m, then 52-53% margin. Gross capex 210 (H2 2026), 650, 450, 80, 35, then ~30m/yr sustaining (7.5% of revenue); EUR 204m grants netted 40/100/64 over 2026-28; remaining net capex EUR 1.19bn at 100%. D&A ~EUR 100m/yr on a ~EUR 1.8bn asset base from 2030. Cash tax 0 through 2028, ramping 5->30% by 2033 as German NOLs (60% minimum-taxation offset) are used. SBC ~EUR 5m/yr. Working capital -10% of revenue change (receivables + product inventory). Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 12x (cyclical commodity).

bull.narrative: 100%-project figures: Lionheart on time and on the BES budget (gross capex 210/620/400/50, net of grants 170/520/336/50), 6kt in 2028 at EUR 16k/t, 20kt in 2029 at 18k, 24kt from 2030 at EUR 20k/t (~US$23k, a 2027+ deficit recovery) + EUR 55m energy = EUR 535m; opex EUR 5,000/t -> ~70% EBITDA margin. Project Ludwig (Phase Two PFS Sept 2026: 21.1ktpa Li2CO3, EUR 1,261m capex, FID 2029) built 2030-32 (capex 250/500/450/100 incl. Lionheart sustaining) and ramping 8kt (2033), 18kt (2034), 21.1kt (2035) at EUR 15k/t carbonate + heat -> group revenue EUR 706m/866m/928m, then +2%/yr; margin dips to 66% in the ramp year then 68%. Attributable share held at 70% for Ludwig too (true share ~85%), so the bull is understated on that leg.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Not the 15/50/35 house default. Bear 35%: proprietary DLE validated only at optimisation-plant scale, a multi-contractor EUR 1.4-1.9bn first-of-kind build already showing drilling setbacks (LSC-1a abandoned), project-finance covenants before any lithium revenue, and a lithium market most forecasters have in surplus into 2027; this is the probability-of-failure leg of a risked NPV. Base 45%: fully financed with binding take-or-pay offtake and all major German permits, so the central case is credible. Bull 20%: needs both on-budget delivery and a price recovery, and most of its upside is a second project (Ludwig) that cannot start before the first works.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is risked_npv: no multiples rule applies; the historical table is reported for context only
